label: heart-s0
summary: The model (training AUC 0.9449) is mostly an additive logistic risk score: its direct linear terms carry most of the discrimination (switching them to their mean drops the training AUC to 0.7356), led by the number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy (1.93 per sd), male sex (1.67), asymptomatic chest pain (1.21) and a flat ST segment (1.05). On top of it sits one interaction: a gate that opens for women with chest pain on exercise and no left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (8 of the 83 training women, 7 of them with the outcome), amplified by a flat ST segment. Exercise angina reaches the prediction through this gate, so it raises a typical woman's risk from 11% to 90% when her ST segment is flat and leaves a typical man's unchanged (23% without, 23% with exercise angina); with a flat segment such a woman is predicted at higher risk than a comparable man (90% against 80%), a reversal fitted to the 7 training women in that regime. A flat ST segment also adds a small bonus through the same path for the 103 flat-segment rows with the gate shut, and a minor always-on unit adds a little risk for hypertrophy (switching it off moves the AUC to 0.9452). Resting blood pressure is ignored, and an ST-T abnormality on the resting ECG is treated like a normal ECG. The annotated model reproduces the network on the training rows to within 3.3e-16.
